sections.title: Situation
sections.prompt: What is the real decision, and which numbers and dates frame it?
criteria: Says the ERP freeze (months 4-9) decides the order of work, not only the value ranking
Derives capacity (84 engineer-months) against demand (102) and the 21-month post-freeze window
Derives today's blended win rate (24.25%) and the $57.6M quoted a month
Names the GM's $3M promise as something to test, and states one thing out of scope

sections.title: Stakeholders
sections.prompt: Who has a stake, what does each want, and how do you bring them along?
criteria: Covers the GM and at least four of the five sponsors, each with a distinct want
Says what BU finance and the VP Field Sales get instead of what they asked for
Includes the ERP programme lead and what you promise them
Ends with one idea that ties the stakeholders together

sections.title: Options
sections.prompt: What are the real ways to fill the year, and how does each fare against the freeze?
criteria: Compares at least two whole-year sequences, not just a list of initiatives
Notices that draft-only Quote Assist writes nothing to ERP and can ship during the freeze
Shows that write-back and AR triage cannot both fit the post-freeze window
Compares options on one table with the same criteria

sections.title: Decision and Trade-offs
sections.prompt: What roadmap do you recommend, what do you give up, and what would change it?
criteria: Makes one clear roadmap with initiatives placed by quarter
Names what is cut or deferred (AR triage, built account briefs) and why
Says which parts are reversible
Sets a dated checkpoint for an ERP slip with a pre-agreed alternative

sections.title: Economics
sections.prompt: What is each initiative worth at month 12, and what does the plan cost?
criteria: Derives win-rate gains from the 4-hour share and turns them into gross profit at 24%
Discounts the speed-to-win link as partly correlation, labelled as an assumption
Gives a floor and an upside run-rate ($1.95M and $3.07M)
Separates new spend against the $900k cap from engineers already on payroll

sections.title: Org and Ownership
sections.prompt: Who owns the roadmap, each initiative and the value number?
criteria: Names a single accountable owner
Makes sponsors own adoption targets, not just requests
Has finance, not the AI team, report the run-rate

sections.title: Plan and Milestones
sections.prompt: What ships when, and where can the plan be stopped or changed?
criteria: Puts something live during the freeze (month 4 to 9)
Has at least one gate with a measurable threshold
Plans for the replica changing at cutover
Includes the month-9 checkpoint before the post-freeze window

sections.title: Risk and Governance
sections.prompt: What could go wrong, and what controls it?
criteria: Quantifies wrong SKU matches a month (about 20,000 at 86%)
Keeps pricing in ERP so AI errors can't leak margin
Has a fallback if the ERP cutover slips
Keeps a rep confirming each line before a quote goes out

sections.title: Metrics
sections.prompt: How do you know the roadmap worked, and what would show it is causing harm?
criteria: Pairs each success metric with a guard metric
Guards win rate with margin per won quote
Measures the speed-to-win effect against non-pilot branches
Ties the headline metric to gross profit, not minutes saved

sections.title: Communication
sections.prompt: What does each audience hear, and how often?
criteria: Gives a one-line message for at least four audiences
Resets the GM's $3M to a floor and an upside before the quarterly review
Tells deferred sponsors when their work starts and why
Sets a cadence and says failed gates are reported too
